summary: v3.5 became an isolated implementation; v2.5 and v3.0 are forbidden as executable dependencies.
lesson: Preserve legacy evidence without allowing mutable cross-version imports.

summary: Real-GPU bridge smoke passed for frozen base/SFT receivers, hidden-state alignment, finite loss and bridge-only gradients.
lesson: A random bridge producing EOS is an expected smoke outcome, not a quality result.

summary: Incompatible cached traces were quarantined after dataset correction; compatible traces were retained only under strict input and provenance hashes.
lesson: Equal split counts do not imply trace compatibility when descriptions or membership change.

summary: Targeted regeneration completed nycc_325 and nycc_775, producing exactly 666/666 validated train+validation traces with zero failures.
lesson: Both final traces passed as new raw generations; the implemented validator-repair path was available but not used for accepted data.

summary: The first learned bridge pilot was moved from a delayed full c-batch allocation to available b-batch-mig slices; both two-slice and one-slice formal attempts later failed.
lesson: Earliest allocation is useful only after the exact formal workload has passed a representative resource smoke.

summary: The first learned pilot loaded successfully on two MIG slices but failed during its first PEFT MLP forward with a PyTorch CUDACachingAllocator NVML_SUCCESS internal assertion.
lesson: Do not equate aggregate MIG memory with a stable multi-device execution path.

summary: One 33-GB MIG slice completed a real typed-SFT receiver backward/update on convenient clusters with finite metrics and about 7.0 GB peak allocation, but this did not predict formal-pilot stability.
lesson: A smoke can pass yet be non-representative; resource qualification must use the formal placement and stress visual sample.

summary: The exact Learned+KL P1 workload failed on one MIG slice during its first selected image's vision-tower PEFT forward with the same NVML allocator assertion.
lesson: Do not run formal bridge training on MIG in this environment; use a compatible full GPU and retain the passing smoke only as bounded evidence.

summary: P1 was resubmitted to one full c-batch GPU with native allocator, fixed CUDA:0 placement, a >=40-GiB resource assertion, and an exact-first-example backward smoke in the same job.
lesson: Qualify the exact formal workload on the retained allocation before consuming the scientific training budget; compare scheduler predictions and cancel slower duplicates.

summary: The v3.5 audit found and fixed stale P1 evaluation paths, allocator drift, weak completion-file checks, and smoke seed drift; 63 tests and all syntax/data/memory gates passed.
lesson: A successful training artifact is a validated set, not a sentinel filename; scheduler node-free counters are not equivalent to an immediately allocatable GPU.

summary: The corrected length-matched single-channel counterfactual evaluator completed 24 image clusters for legacy v1 and v2. Both methods remained inconclusive: no stable positive use of all conflict/local/global channels was shown, and the result is not a method-level latent rejection.
lesson: A corrected counterfactual pilot can remove a length/softmax confound without supplying enough statistical power for a method-level conclusion; keep semantic review separate from caption and preference training.

summary: The first Phase A3 real-trace smoke stopped before forward/backward because a valid 492-token global HOMER target exceeded the configured 384-token bound. The configuration was raised to 768 and the replacement smoke subsequently passed.
lesson: A latent training claim cannot be made from an unexecuted smoke; preserve the failed log, fix the bound without truncation, and close the incident only after the exact real-trace validator passes.

summary: v3.5 is explicitly latent-only. The immediate sequence is A3 replacement smoke, bridge-only 64/24 semantic recovery, and outer semantic confirmation; DPO/SimPO/IPO and preference jobs belong to the superseded v2.5 plan and are disabled.
lesson: Do not let stale preference automation override the active latent experiment; update canonical plan and volatile working state whenever the phase boundary changes.

summary: The corrected Phase A3 real-trace engineering smoke completed on one full H100 with max_target_tokens=768. Two stress-selected real clusters completed forward/backward, channel-wise counterfactual and contextual InfoNCE paths; the two 7B policies remained frozen and the bridge update was finite and non-zero.
lesson: The token-bound configuration incident is closed, but a two-example smoke is only an execution gate; formal 64/24 semantic recovery and held-out caption evaluation remain scientifically open.

summary: Formal Phase A3 channel-balanced semantic recovery completed 5 epochs and 80 optimizer steps on 64 train/24 validation clusters with only the bridge trainable. Validation NLL and contextual InfoNCE retrieval improved, engineering invariants passed, but all channel-wise bootstrap intervals for matched/shuffled gaps crossed zero; the result is an engineering-valid mechanism pilot, not a latent failure or caption-quality gain.
lesson: A successful training run still requires a sealed outer cluster confirmation before any caption or preference claim; record the gate state separately from loss improvements.

summary: The first local full-suite command used system pytest and failed collection because torch/yaml were absent; the locked .venv/bin/python -m pytest rerun passed all 75 tests.
lesson: Always bind verification to the project Python 3.12 environment; a system-tool failure is not model or method evidence.

summary: After the clean outer-confirmation preflight, a 2-cluster real-trace smoke was retained as job 6708041 on c-batch with a 10-minute walltime. b-batch gave a later 2026-09-10 reservation for the same request; its duplicate 6708042 was canceled. Interactive groups were not used because they reject batch execution or were later.
lesson: Use the earliest compatible full-GPU reservation, but do not switch to MIG or an interactive allocation after prior allocator failures; keep one smoke job and inspect the scheduler estimate before adding a full run.

summary: The c-batch smoke reservation was tightened from the canceled 10-minute probe 6708041 to 5-minute probe 6708044; the scheduler retained the same earliest estimated start (2026-09-04 11:00). This is a walltime reduction, not an experiment change.
lesson: Use the shortest walltime justified by the measured 2-cluster smoke while preserving the exact command and full-GPU requirement.

summary: Replaced shared GPU probe 6708044 with b-batch node-allocated simplex smoke 6708113 after PJM rejected node+gpu and gpu+exec-policy=simplex combinations.
lesson: On GENKAI, request node=1 in GPU-capable b-batch for node-exclusive allocation; the node profile supplies GPUs and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 preserves a deterministic single-device process.

summary: Submitted the 40-cluster outer semantic confirmation as a b-batch node-allocated simplex job 6708118 after the node-exclusive smoke passed; scheduler estimates 2026-09-05 12:00 start for the one-hour request.
lesson: The node-exclusive GPU mode is valid and reproducible, but a longer one-hour allocation may receive a later reservation than a short smoke; do not replace it with MIG or shared execution after the allocator incident.

summary: A3's near-zero matched/shuffled log-probability gaps were reclassified as causal-channel-use unproven, not latent failure. A4 adds target-only channel visibility, a no-image semantic-recovery prompt, donor-side counterfactual reconstruction, and a dedicated real-trace validator while preserving A3 unchanged.
lesson: A loss value such as softplus(margin-gap) is not a semantic gap; before scaling, isolate the causal channel, remove image shortcuts, require donor reconstruction, and run a real-trace GPU smoke on a clean commit.

summary: A4 smoke 6711036 was terminated by an erroneous pjdel while clean preflight was still running; PJM recorded signal 15 and no report was produced. No scientific conclusion is attached.
lesson: A transiently empty pjstat listing is not a terminal state; confirm completion through pjstat history and the .stats terminal fields before deleting or classifying a GPU job.

summary: A4 replacement real-trace smoke 6711052 completed on one node-exclusive b-batch H100 in 4m03s. Clean preflight, CUDA resource check, two real traces, target-only one-hot channel masks, donor reconstruction, finite bridge gradient/update, and frozen-policy invariants all passed; no scientific training or caption generation was performed.
lesson: A real-trace engineering pass unlocks the bridge-only pilot but does not establish causal semantic or caption-quality benefit; keep the formal semantic gate and downstream evaluation separate.

summary: A4 formal job 6711074 was initially queued on c-batch, while the duplicate b-batch node-exclusive job 6711070 was canceled to obey the earliest-safe-start policy. Before 6711074 executed forward, script review found that the generic entrypoint lacked the A4 semantic gate and used a stale output contract; 6711074 was canceled and no scientific result exists.
lesson: Earliest queue time is subordinate to method-specific provenance correctness: inspect the actual job entrypoint and output/gate contract before accepting a queued formal job; cancel before forward if the protocol is wrong, then submit only a corrected clean script.

summary: The A4 formal entrypoint now uses one c-batch GPU, a fresh output directory, A4 resource smoke and validator before training, and dynamically reads its own semantic_gate.json after bridge-only training. A regression test prevents reintroducing the generic-script/stale-output mistake.
lesson: A smoke-passed method is not submission-ready until the formal script itself enforces the method-specific gate, clean provenance and non-overlapping output path; guarantee those engineering invariants before measuring scientific effectiveness.

summary: Corrected A4 bridge-only formal pilot 6711109 was submitted from clean commit e6763d6a2314fd2da7f1ee2ec9a1512710d7eb2f on c-batch with one full GPU. PJM reports QUE with estimated start 2026-09-05 12:00; no forward or scientific result has occurred yet.
lesson: Record the exact submitted job and preflight commit immediately; a queued status is not a training result, and the first scientific checkpoint is the post-training A4 semantic gate.

summary: The current public-route real-trace smoke was kept fail-closed while GPU groups were audited. b-batch node=1 job 6753645 was canceled at an estimated next-day start because no b-batch node was free; a-batch probe 6753705 was canceled because its free nodes expose no GPU resource; a b-inter node+gpu override was rejected before job creation.
lesson: Fastest-resource selection must check batch permission, GPU visibility, compatible sharing/node policy and actual PJM START_DATE together. Aggregate GPU capacity or free CPU nodes is not enough; after recording this audit, submit exactly one validated b-batch node=1 smoke from a clean commit.
